what: Stage 4 KV cache: cached decode vs Stage 3 full-recompute decode
model: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (bf16 weights, fp32 activations + fp32 KV cache)
prompt: prompt3 (12 tokens), greedy; decode tok/s at two lengths to show that the cache win GROWS with length (recompute is O(T) per token, cached is ~O(1) model work)
equivalence: cached == recompute token streams on all 5 prompts, CPU + GPU (mine and cublas); CPU per-step logits bit-identical (diff 0)
sanitizer: 4/4 clean on the GPU cache path (memcheck/initcheck/synccheck/racecheck)

findings.naive_kernels: cache wins 2.4x at n=32 and 5.5x at n=256 (15.7 vs 2.86); recompute decode slows badly with length (12.4 -> 2.9), cached stays far more stable (29 -> 15.7). The KV cache is the biggest algorithmic win when the matmuls dominate.
findings.cublas: cache barely moves it (80 vs 78 at n=32, 24 vs 23 at n=256). With cuBLAS the GEMMs are already fast enough that decode is dominated by per-step OVERHEAD (600KB logits copy + implicit sync every step, ~220 serialized kernel launches per token, host-side rope + CPU argmax over 151936). Removing redundant GEMM work doesn't help when GEMM wasn't the bottleneck. That overhead, not the cache, is the next thing to attack.
findings.length_dependence: even cached decode is not perfectly flat (attention_cached is O(cache_len) and runs badly-occupied on ~14 threads), but the per-token MODEL work is now constant vs recompute's linear growth, which is the whole point.
